answer: Each identity delivers one walnut crate to a shale depot and locks a 40-credit bond. The depot weighs, seals the crate, and posts its weight and seal in the shale ledger. A hollow or resealed crate burns the bond and voids the identity. The depot weighs one crate per minute, so the k-th crate waits k minutes; unweighed crates expire after 360 minutes and burn their bonds, so 1,000 fakes pay 20,000 freight and lock 40,000 in bonds while at most 360 clear in an epoch. A rented-crate ring fails: one seal binds one crate to one key. An honest agent pays 20 and reclaims its bond.
